svg.title: Trace context propagation
svg.desc: A W3C traceparent entering at the server filter and flowing outward: the SERVER span published to Laravel Context as firefly.trace_id and firefly.span_id, an INTERNAL span on each CQRS message, a PRODUCER span on publish and a CONSUMER span on delivery around an EDA envelope whose headers carry the traceparent — the in-memory and queue buses, the RabbitMQ, Kafka and Postgres publishers and the outbox relay all reach that seam, while SubscriberRegistrySink traces the delivery side for every broker consumer — and a CLIENT span on every outbound Http call that injects it again, landing on every log line, on the httpexchanges endpoint and on the dashboard.
svg.text: One traceparent, five boundaries, three places you can read it
packages/observability/src/Web/{TracingFilter.php, HttpClientTracingMiddleware.php} · packages/observability/src/Tracing/W3CTraceContextPropagator.php
packages/observability/src/{Cqrs/TracerCqrsTracing.php, Eda/TracerEdaTracing.php, Logging/TraceContextLogProcessor.php, Boot/HttpClientTracingPass.php} · packages/eda/src/Tracing/BrokerTracing.php
Inbound request header
traceparent: 00-{32 hex trace-id}-{16 hex span-id}-01
absent → a new root trace starts here
TracingFilter — #[Order(-110)], the outermost ordered filter in the chain
W3CTraceContextPropagator::extract($request->headers->all()) → the remote parent · startSpan($method, SpanKind::Server, …, $parent)
renamed to `GET /orders/{id}` once the router has matched · http.request.method, url.path, url.scheme, server.address, http.route, http.response.status_code, firefly.correlation_id · ERROR on 5xx
Laravel Context and Request::$attributes
firefly.trace_id · firefly.span_id — the one place everything downstream reads the ids from
CQRS · in-process
CqrsTracing seam in firefly/cqrs (NoOpCqrsTracing by
default), filled by TracerCqrsTracing.
INTERNAL span per command and per query,
named by the message's short class name
firefly.cqrs.kind · firefly.cqrs.message
nothing to carry — it nests under whatever is current
gated by firefly.observability.tracing.cqrs.enabled, which
is on by default under the master tracing gate.
EDA · across the transport
EdaTracing seam in firefly/eda, filled by TracerEdaTracing. Reached from the in-memory
and queue buses, from SubscriberRegistrySink (the sink every broker consumer feeds), from
RabbitMqEventPublisher, KafkaEventPublisher and PostgresEventPublisher (both its writers),
and from OutboxRelay, whose traceConsume() keeps the relay hop on the row's own trace.
PRODUCER `publish <destination>` writes traceparent/tracestate into the headers
CONSUMER `process <destination>` on delivery reads them back and continues that trace
gated by firefly.observability.tracing.eda.enabled; firefly.eda.tracing.brokers.enabled=false
downgrades the three broker publishers alone to the no-op, so none of ours is stamped.
Outbound HTTP
HttpClientTracingMiddleware, installed on the Http
factory by HttpClientTracingPass at boot.
CLIENT span · inject() writes traceparent on the
PSR-7 request — url.path, never url.full
ERROR at ≥ 400 or on a rejection
works under Http::fake(): global middleware is outermost
gated by firefly.observability.tracing.http-client.enabled,
read by the boot pass rather than by a bean condition.
The next service's own TracingFilter extracts the same traceparent — and the trace continues, across the process boundary, with no shared code
The propagator speaks W3C Trace Context over a plain header map, with no SDK involved: version `ff` and all-zero ids are rejected, a future version is read for its first four fields.
Where the ids land
Every log line
TraceContextLogProcessor adds trace_id and span_id
to each record, beside the correlation and request ids.
firefly.logging.structured.format: json · ecs · logstash
attached per channel at resolution time, so a channel
built after boot with Log::build() gets neither.
/actuator/httpexchanges
HttpExchangeFilter (-100) runs INSIDE the tracing filter, so the span already exists
when it records the exchange, and it reads the traceId TracingFilter published off
Request::$attributes rather than off Context.
every row carries the trace it belonged to
a ring of the last 100 by default — httpexchanges.capacity, clamped to [1, 10000]
The admin dashboard
firefly/admin renders the same exchanges page
server-side from the actuator registries — no
second data path, no JavaScript fetch.
read its access model before exposing it: the
dashboard ships no authentication of its own.
What is actually recording
The shipped default is NoOpTracer: non-recording spans, an invalid SpanContext, currentSpan() of null — every instrumentation site tests
$span->context()->isValid() before publishing ids. The OpenTelemetry adapter binds itself when the SDK is installed and firefly.observability.tracing.enabled is on.
Both seams follow the CqrsMetrics shape: an interface in the owning package with a no-op default behind #[ConditionalOnMissingBean], and observability's
#[Order(500)] auto-configuration registering the real implementation first. Neither firefly/cqrs nor firefly/eda depends on firefly/observability.
A span whose end is deferred past the frame that started it — the CLIENT span of an Http call ends in the promise's then() — calls deactivate() as soon as its
synchronous part is over, which is what keeps every request of an Http::pool() a sibling rather than a chain.
